title: SU(3) d- and f-symbol contraction identities as adjoint-tensor reconstruction
expression_sketch: Adjoint indices a,b,c,d,e in {1,...,8}. Structure constants of su(3) in the Gell-Mann basis: f_abc totally antisymmetric with f_123=1, f_147=f_246=f_257=f_345=-f_156=-f_367=1/2, f_458=f_678=sqrt(3)/2 (all others vanishing up to permutation); d_abc totally symmetric with d_118=d_228=d_338=-d_888=1/sqrt(3), d_448=d_558=d_668=d_778=-1/(2*sqrt(3)), d_146=d_157=d_256=d_344=d_355=-d_247=-d_366=-d_377=1/2. Quadratic contractions (Haber 2021 eqs. (26)--(27) at N=3; Macfarlane--Sudbery--Weisz 1968): Sum_{b,c=1}^{8} f_abc*f_dbc = 3*delta(a,d); Sum_{b,c} d_abc*d_dbc = (5/3)*delta(a,d); Sum_{b,c} f_abc*d_dbc = 0. Jacobi: Sum_e (f_abe*f_ecd + f_cbe*f_aed + f_dbe*f_ace) = 0. SU(3)-only reconstruction of Kronecker products (Haber eqs. (75)--(76); Macfarlane et al.): 3*Sum_e d_abe*d_cde - Sum_e f_ace*f_bde - Sum_e f_ade*f_bce == delta(a,c)*delta(b,d) + delta(a,d)*delta(b,c) - delta(a,b)*delta(c,d); and Sum_e (d_abe*d_cde + d_ace*d_bde + d_ade*d_bce) == (1/3)*(delta(a,b)*delta(c,d)+delta(a,c)*delta(b,d)+delta(a,d)*delta(b,c)).
latent_structure: The totally symmetric d-tensor and antisymmetric f-tensor of su(3) are the invariant generators of the adjoint. Their quadratic contractions reconstruct the adjoint Killing form (3 delta) and the d-metric (5/3 delta). The N=3 characteristic identities reconstruct the three Kronecker pairings of 8x8 as linear combinations of d*d and f*f, an invariant-basis rewrite not available for general SU(N).

function_domains.f: Totally antisymmetric real structure constants of su(3) in the Gell-Mann basis, with the PDG/Wikipedia nonzero list.
function_domains.d: Totally symmetric real d-symbols of su(3) in the same basis.

nonzero_conditions.statement: N=3 is nonzero and N^2-4=5 is nonzero, so Haber coefficients N and (N^2-4)/N = 5/3 are defined in Q.
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Haber 2021 eqs. (26)--(27); Macfarlane--Sudbery--Weisz, Commun. Math. Phys. 11 (1968) 77

positivity_conditions.statement: sqrt(3) in f_458, f_678 and in the listed d_**8 entries is the positive real square root.
positivity_conditions.label: DECLARED
positivity_conditions.source: Wikipedia Gell-Mann matrices / PDG SU(3) table of f_abc and d_abc

branch_conventions: sqrt denotes the principal nonnegative real square root on (0,oo); only sqrt(3) appears.
source_provenance: A. J. Macfarlane, A. Sudbery, P. H. Weisz, On Gell-Mann's lambda-matrices, d- and f-tensors, octets, and parametrizations of SU(3), Commun. Math. Phys. 11 (1968) 77-90.
Particle Data Group, Review of Particle Physics, Table of f_abc and d_abc.

derived_conditions.statement: The quadratic identities f_abc f_abd = N delta_cd and d_abc d_abd = ((N^2-4)/N) delta_cd hold for all SU(N); the two characteristic identities (75)--(76) are special to N=3 and do not extend.
derived_conditions.label: DECLARED
derived_conditions.source: Haber 2021 section 5: 'two additional identities ... special to the case of N=3 and do not generalize'

derived_conditions.statement: Einstein summation on a repeated adjoint index is the explicit finite sum over {1,...,8}.
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: finite-dimensional Lie-algebra tensors; Haber index ranges a=1..N^2-1

public_source: Macfarlane--Sudbery--Weisz Commun. Math. Phys. 11 (1968); Haber SciPost Lect. Notes 21 (2021) eqs. (26)--(27), (75)--(76)
why_not_cse_lgg: A generic 8x8x8 array of structure constants has no CSE that yields the two quadratic Casimirs or the N=3 Kronecker reconstruction. LGG cannot invent the d-tensor as an invariant generator of SU(3)/Z_3. The compact object is an adjoint-invariant basis rewrite.
proposer_leak_risk: Hide d-symbol, f-symbol, adjoint Casimir, Macfarlane, characteristic equation of su(3). Show the numerical 8-index contractions only.
notes: Purely algebraic over Q(sqrt(3)). The N=3 reconstruction identities are the headline obligation; the general-N contractions are the shared latent. Distinct from Levi-Civita eps-delta (SO(3) rank-3) and from Pauli completeness.
